CSIS 200.course_name: Introduction to Critical Studies in Gender and Sexuality
CSIS 200.description: Introductory course that emphasizes how sexuality and gender intersect with race, class, ability, and geography. This course is recommended for students who have completed GRSJ_V 101.

CSIS 300.description: A multi-disciplinary course that explores the study of sexuality, including lesbian, gay, bisexual, heterosexual, and transgender issues and related topics. This course is recommended for students who have completed CSIS_V 200.

CSIS 301.description: How race, citizenship, gender, sexuality, culture and dis/ability are materially and socially constructed together to give meaning to the category trans*. (Trans*: transgender, transsexual, gender variant and other articulations.) This course is recommended for students who have completed CSIS_V 200.

CSIS 450.course_name: Topics in Critical Studies in Sexuality
CSIS 450.description: A thematic course, which explores current questions and issues in relation to the study of sexuality. Topics may vary from year to year.

CSIS 490.description: Designed to allow a student to develop an individual course of study in a specific area as approved by a faculty member affiliated with the CSIS program.
